description: Canonical metric templates (design doc Section 4). facts[] are row-level helper expressions owned by one entity; metrics[] are aggregate-level. A metric with kind='derived' MUST be emitted as a YAML top-level derived metric (never table-scoped) because it composes metrics owned by two different entities across a non-1:1 relationship -- see implementation-findings.md Finding 1. Placeholder syntax: {{Entity.attribute}} resolves to the mapped physical column expression on Entity's resolved logical table; {{Entity}} alone resolves to just the resolved logical table alias (lowercased).

variables.name: on_time_tolerance_days
variables.description: Days of grace period before a late delivery counts as late.

facts.name: is_on_time
facts.expr_template: CASE WHEN {{Transaction.delivery_date}} <= DATEADD('day', on_time_tolerance_days, {{Transaction.promised_delivery_date}}) THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END
facts.description: Binary: 1 if delivered on or before the promised date (+ tolerance). Public so filters like 'late shipments' can use WHERE is_on_time = 0.

facts.name: is_in_full
facts.description: Binary: 1 if this transaction alone covers the full ordered quantity of its demand line. References DemandLine.ordered_qty directly -- valid because this is a row-level fact and DemandLine is at lower granularity (FK lookup), per Snowflake's row-level expression rules. NOTE: ordered_qty is otherwise only used inside SUM() aggregations, so it has no standalone row-level declaration on its own table by default -- cross_refs tells the instantiation engine to auto-generate a passthrough fact for it (see Finding in implementation-findings.md: 'invalid identifier' error otherwise).

facts.name: is_defect_free
facts.description: Binary: 1 if no defects were found in this transaction.

facts.name: lead_time_days
facts.description: Days from order placement to this transaction's delivery. References Demand.order_date -- valid via the transitive FK path Transaction -> DemandLine -> Demand.

metrics.name: total_ordered_qty
metrics.description: Total quantity ordered across demand lines.

metrics.name: on_time_delivery_rate
metrics.description: Percentage of shipments delivered on or before the promised date.

metrics.name: otif_rate
metrics.expr_template: AVG(CASE WHEN is_on_time = 1.0 AND is_in_full = 1.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100
metrics.description: Percentage of shipments that are both on-time and in-full (per-shipment grain). Debatable: could instead be defined per-order-line or per-order (see design doc Section 4).

metrics.name: avg_lead_time_days
metrics.description: Average days from order placement to delivery.

metrics.name: supplier_defect_rate
metrics.description: Percentage of received units found defective. Debatable: unit-level (chosen) vs. shipment-level binary.

metrics.name: perfect_order_rate
metrics.expr_template: AVG(CASE WHEN is_on_time = 1.0 AND is_in_full = 1.0 AND is_defect_free = 1.0 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * 100
metrics.description: Percentage of shipments that are on-time, in-full, and defect-free.

metrics.name: fill_rate
metrics.description: Ratio of total shipped quantity to total ordered quantity, as a percentage. MUST be a view-level derived metric: DemandLine -> Transaction is one-to-many, so composing this as a table-scoped metric owned by Transaction fans out (see implementation-findings.md Finding 1). Debatable variant: ratio-of-quantity (chosen) vs. binary per-line-complete.

metrics.name: order_cycle_time_days
metrics.description: Average days from order placement to the last (final) delivery for that order. Demand is coarser grain than Transaction (many transactions per order via DemandLine), so this uses nested aggregation (MAX per order, then AVG across orders) -- valid as a table-scoped metric per Snowflake's 'higher granularity reference' rule for metrics, unlike fill_rate which combines two independently-owned metrics.
